chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Ribat, from Isa ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who gave his wife the choice (of divorce), and she chose herself (to be divorced), so she was separated from him. He said: No, this was a matter specific to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), who was commanded to do so. And if they had chosen themselves, they would have been divorced.
O Prophet, say to your wives, 'If you should desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, that I may provide for you and give you a gracious release.'
Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah said: With this report, we take the ruling regarding the choice (of divorce).

key_terms.الْخِيَار: The option or choice, specifically referring to the right of a wife to choose between staying in or leaving the marriage.
key_terms.سَرَاحًا جَمِيلًا: A gracious release, a Quranic term for divorce without penalty or waiting period in this context.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's right of choice (al-khiyar) and the general ruling for men giving their wives the choice of divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies that the specific legal mechanism of 'al-khiyar' (where the wife's choice finalizes the divorce immediately) was a unique privilege granted exclusively to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by divine command, as evidenced by the citation of Surah Al-Ahzab. For the general Muslim community, while the principle of choice remains valid, the immediate effect of the wife's selection is derived from this prophetic precedent. The narration underscores the distinction between the Prophet's special status and the general application of divorce law in Shia jurisprudence.
